title: “Your thoughts are too small for what God is doing.”
paragraphs: “Your thoughts are too small for what God is doing.”

Isaiah 55:8 (ESV)
“For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, declares the Lord.”

You prayed.
But heaven stayed quiet.

You planned.
But everything fell apart.

And now you’re asking—
“Lord, what are You doing?”

Here’s the tension:
God is not confused.
You are just not seeing the full picture.

Because His thoughts…
are not your thoughts.

His ways…
cut through places you’re afraid to walk.

We want clarity.
God builds trust.

We want control.
God writes redemption.

And sometimes the delay, the denial, the detour—
it’s not rejection.

It’s protection.
It’s preparation.
It’s positioning.
But here’s what we miss…

We judge God by the moment.
God is working in eternity.

You see the chapter.
He holds the whole story.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because the same God whose ways are higher—
stepped down into our mess through Jesus Christ.

He didn’t stay distant.
He entered our confusion.
Carried our sin.
Died our death.

So when you don’t understand His plan—
you can trust His heart.
The cross proves it.

You may not know why right now.
But you can know Who is in control.

And His ways?
They lead to life.

Don’t shrink God to fit your understanding.
Let Him lift you into His purpose.
From confusion to clarity — because Jesus rewrites everything.
